title: In less than 2 weeks the world decides if I just set the bar, or am the latest victim of AI Psychosis
author: wasitworthitdev
selftext:
It won't matter the programming I did before the us government let companies' setup their own power plants to feed their AI/data centers or the games I made with & without an assistant that you can't outwork period. It won't matter that it's my fifth game. And it won't matter the tech company pledges at the president's table. It won't matter how many billionaires\\trillionaires said 'Yes, Sir' in that room.

At the end of the day, it's still about the lore building and the design.   
  
At the end of the day, it won't matter the endless hours you still had to put in.   
  
At the end of the day, it's still just the player and the game.

I know I've set the bar, my fellows dev's you can't even imagine how long I've been up here and I say that amongst indie developers; it's meaningless. But! The game's too good to deny. I'm the cornerstone the builder can't refuse. I'm prepared to be that dev, because that's exactly what the 20 hours of work every single day for the past decade has led to. This title.

[wozitdev's 3D Sniper - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@wozitdevs3DSniper) \- If you must see it for yourself. Me? I expect silence. When Jesus is prepared to shake the earth, then he will rest upon his footstool. I try to make it last forever, in a year you'll be able to make ""that game"" in a day, but you won't be able to make this game in your lifetime. Next time, you might be saying "I'll build something better", but you won't have this year; there simply isn't enough time. Honestly, the Job was left to me and that's my favorite book in the bible to read to people.

replies.author: pikuray
replies.body: One of the central themes in the anime Naruto is that with enough hard work, it's possible to progress far beyond what they initially thought possible. The best example of that might be Rock Lee, who doesn't have the ability to produce chakra, which in that world is basically like having a profound disability, but through training his body he was able to do well for himself.

replies.author: Vivid-Snow-2089
replies.body:
Yes, well, promising a person who is blind that they can become an expert manga colorist isn't a great thing. This applies to a lot of things. A whole generation (or two) has been promised that they can grow up to do and be anything they want, when in reality that's not realistic. There is great pride and celebration of people who strive beyond what was they were capable of not because it's common or normal, but because they are the exception. In reality most people fall short of many of their aspirations and that's fine, it's often said that its better to shoot for the moon and reach a mountain summit than to stay under a rock and never make an attempt...

But promising success and that it will always be achieved? That's wrong
